source.title: On the Steering Dimensionality of Refusal in Language Models
source.authors: Han-Gong Wang; Erik Miehling; Dennis Wei; K. Ramamurthy; Huan Zhang

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether refusal steering is one-dimensional and reports that the required dimensionality depends on context; general-context refusal is not reliably controlled even with 5-dimensional subspaces.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative outcomes for its steering interventions in the text, but the figures' numerical values are not present in the supplied text. It also describes contrastive examples used to construct subspaces; those construction data are not outcomes and are not rows.
record.test_reason: Replicates Arditi-style harmful-minus-harmless addition and ablation on two instruct models, sweeping subspace dimension k∈{1,2,3,5}. It finds safety refusal is 1-dim steerable. Instructed general-context refusal is not controlled by that direction, nor by response-semantic subspaces up to 5 dims. That argues V1 needs restating by refusal context and bears on V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Safety-alignment-triggered refusal is 1-dim steerable, and several distinct directions give comparable control. Refusal in general contexts has richer geometry that even 5-dim subspaces fail to control. Refusal geometry is context-dependent.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-versus-harmless contrastive activations for safety refusal and tests additive steering plus directional ablation, but generalizes to multidimensional subspaces and also studies response-semantic contrasts. It intervenes at selected layers rather than every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on refusal context, model, subspace construction, and dimension. For Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, ablation at k ∈ {3, 5} begins to harm coherence; Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct general-refusal ablation is ineffective across four settings.
record.peer_reviewed: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026), Workshop: Interpretability as a Science
record.problems: Only two instruction-tuned models are evaluated. The supplied text gives qualitative figure descriptions but no numerical figure values or uncertainty estimates. Response coherence is assessed, but broad general capabilities are not. Ablation is limited to layers spanning one-third to two-thirds of model depth by default.
record.rows_left_out: No separately quantified figure values were available in the supplied text. The text does not state separate numeric outcomes for every method, dimension, or general-refusal evaluation setting, so no such values were inferred.

untested.parts: Broad capability preservation: only response coherence is judged, no capability benchmarks. Ablation covers only middle layers, not every layer and position.
Affine or cone descriptions are not tested directly. Only linear subspaces built by K-Means, PCA or SVD are compared.
No weight edit or abliterated released model.
Harmfulness judgment is not measured separately from refusal.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct.
No comparison of training regimes or stages.

missing.what: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, safety refusal with PCA construction: the text names only K-Means and SVD as effective, implying PCA was not.
missing.locator: Section 4.1, 'can be reliably controlled using different steering subspaces'; Figure 2

missing.what: Incoherence ratio (%) under safety-direction addition and ablation per k and method, the only response-quality check relevant to 'other abilities kept'.
Numeric steerability values per k, method and evaluation setting (four ablation settings).

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. General-context subspaces use a response-semantic contrast generated by Gemma-4-31B and judged by Qwen3.8-27B, so they are not the V1 difference-in-means direction; those rows bear on V4 only. The only evidence for the general/safety distinction at V1's direction is R13/R14, where the 'refusal' is instruction-induced. Only two small instruct models are tested, there are 50 examples per setting, and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether all other abilities are largely intact; coherence is assessed, but broad capabilities are not. Ablation is applied to layers spanning one-third to two-thirds of model depth by default, not every layer and position.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration experiment.
No jailbreak suppression or training against ablation experiment.
Does not test affine or cone descriptions directly; it compares steering-subspace dimensions and construction methods.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or model-variant transfer experiment.
No comparison of refusal-training methods, timing, or training stages.

relation.reason: Its own addition and ablation experiments bear directly on V1 (single DIM direction) and V4 (multi-dimensional subspaces).

tranche.reason: It replicates Arditi's DIM addition and ablation (K-Means k=1). It then argues refusal geometry is context-dependent: one direction controls safety refusal but not general-context refusal. That bears on how V1 and V4 should be stated.

source_check.notes: All results are figure-only and qualitative; there are no random-direction controls and no benchmarks. The only capability check is a coherence judge (Qwen3.8-27B), with n=50 per evaluation set and 3 rollouts each. The Fig. 3 caption also marks Qwen ablation at k in {3,5} as losing coherence, which no row records. No row records PCA on Llama, which the text implies was not effective. The appendix prompts are the study's own data-generation and judge prompts, not instructions to the reader.

statements.problem: No problem for this study. The cited result is the safety-derived subspace, possibly at k>1, not only a single direction.
Correct for this study. Fig. 3's caption, for the safety-alignment subspace on Qwen, also greys out k in {3,5} for coherence loss, so the cost may not be limited to the general-context subspace.

statements.correction: Text: on Llama-3.1-8B, only K-Means and SVD are named as giving effective control; PCA is not reported as effective.
statements.problem: Correct. 'Did not work' for PCA on Llama is an inference from the text's 'whereas'; the text does not state it. Near-saturation at k=1 is stated for additive steering. Directions are not shown to be geometrically distinct (no cosines).
No problem. General-context refusal is instructed refusal (refuse-all-requests prompts), and the safety subspace gives little suppression of it.

statements.correction: 2610.04245: safety refusal is controlled at k=1 by both addition and ablation. Llama-3.1-8B general-context refusal: additive steerability saturates beyond k=3 (K-Means); ablation ineffective in all four settings up to k=5.
statements.problem: For this study, the statement contrasts refusal types (safety vs general), not operations. For safety refusal, addition (R1-R5) and ablation (R6-R9) both work at k=1. The only operation difference is general refusal on Llama: addition saturates beyond k=3 (R10) while ablation is ineffective up to k=5 (R11).
